edition_notes: Designed by Wolfgang Warsch; published by Nürnberger-Spielkarten-Verlag GmbH (NSV); 2-4 players, age 8+, approx. 20 min.

items.rule: All players form a single cooperative team; the game is played with 2-4 players.
With 2 players use levels 1-12, 2 lives and 1 throwing star.
With 3 players use levels 1-10, 3 lives and 1 throwing star.
With 4 players use levels 1-8, 4 lives and 1 throwing star.
Lives and throwing stars in use are laid out openly on the table; the remaining ones are set aside at the table edge for later rewards.
Level cards in use are stacked in ascending order as an open deck with level 1 on top; unused levels go back in the box.
Shuffle the 100 number cards (1-100) and deal each player one card for level 1, held hidden from the others; the rest form a face-down draw pile at the table edge.
At level N each player is dealt N cards; for each new level all 100 cards are reshuffled and each player gets one more card than in the previous level.
Before each level starts, every player who is ready places one hand palm down on the table; when all are ready, hands are lifted and play begins.
There are no turns: whoever believes they hold the lowest card currently available plays it face up onto a single open stack in the centre.
Cards are played one at a time and each player must always play the lowest card in their hand first; a player holding consecutive-low cards may play them one after the other.
Players must not disclose or show their card values; no consultation and no secret signals are allowed.
Any player may say "stop" at any time to interrupt play; everyone places a hand on the table to refocus, then removes hands and play continues.
If all cards are played in correct ascending order, the level is completed; the top level card is put in the box and the next level is prepared.
Rewards for completing levels 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9 are shown at the bottom right of the level card: 1 life or 1 throwing star (level 2 gives a throwing star), taken from the table edge.
The team can hold at most 5 lives and 3 throwing stars.
Error: if a card is played in the wrong order, whoever holds a lower card halts the game immediately and the team loses 1 life (a life card goes to the table edge).
After an error, all held cards lower than the last card played are set aside (discarded); then the team refocuses and continues the current level without restarting it.

Throwing star: any player may suggest using one by raising a hand; if all players agree, each player discards their lowest card face up to one side and one throwing star is set aside, then everyone refocuses and play continues.
The game ends in collective victory when the team completes all levels in the stack.
The game ends in failure when the team loses its last life.
There are no points; success is measured only by completing all levels before losing all lives.
Everyone wins together if all levels are completed; everyone loses together if the last life is lost.
Blind mode: after completing all levels, the team may continue by restarting at level 1 with its remaining lives and throwing stars, playing all cards face down on the stack.
In blind mode the stack is turned over at the end of the level to check the order; a mistake costs one life, and other rules are unchanged; the goal is to see how many levels can be completed blind.
